text: **dsh-opencode-session-header**（DSH 模型插件）：为 opencode-go 开头的路由添加按会话区分的 x-opencode-session 请求头。插件在模型请求交给 pi-ai 前复制选项并补入会话标识，支持 auto、uuid、id 三种值模式，也可让无会话标识的辅助调用继承发起会话。状态端点展示挂接情况和诊断信息，卸载时会恢复钩子。适合使用 OpenCode Go 网关的 DSH 用户，无需额外 API Key。

**dsh-opencode-session-header** adds a per-conversation x-opencode-session header to DSH opencode-go routes. It copies options before adding the conversation ID, supports three value modes, and can inherit IDs for auxiliary calls. A status endpoint reports hook state. No extra key is required.
让 OpenCode Go 的每段 DSH 对话都带上各自的会话请求头。
DSH 调用 OpenCode Go 网关时提示缺少会话 ID，怎么补上？
想按对话区分模型网关的缓存路由。
有没有办法只给 opencode-go 开头的模型路由加会话头？
让辅助标题或压缩请求也沿用发起它的会话标识。
我需要查看 DSH 插件是否成功挂接模型适配器。
How can I attach a conversation-specific session header to OpenCode Go requests?
I need to route each DSH conversation to its own gateway cache bucket.
**dsh-opencode-session-header** 的功能「会话请求头」：模型调用进入 pi-ai 前，插件把会话标识写入 x-opencode-session，并复制请求选项避免改动原对象。
**dsh-opencode-session-header** 的功能「路由范围」：插件按模型路由名判断是否以 opencode-go 开头，只对匹配路由添加请求头，其他路由保持原样。
**dsh-opencode-session-header** 的功能「请求头值模式」：用户可选 auto、uuid 或 id；auto 会按模型协议选择会话标识形式，供网关识别当前对话。
**dsh-opencode-session-header** 的功能「状态诊断」：通过同源 GET 状态端点查看挂接的适配器、匹配路由、调用计数和诊断信息。

dsh-opencode-session-header README · dsh-opencode-session-header：A DeepSeek Harness plugin that puts a stable **per-conversation**
`x-opencode-session` header on every inference request a **`opencode-go…`** route
makes — the builtin `opencode-go`, this deployment's `opencode-go-custom`, and any
sibling route added later — so OpenCode's Go / Zen gateway stops answering
`400 MissingSessionID` and can route each conversation to its own cache bucket.

It replaces the deployment-wide patch script: same fix, same header channel, but

dsh-opencode-session-header README · Why a plugin is needed at all：The gateway requires a **per-conversation** id. DSH already knows it and hands it
to pi-ai as `GenerateOptions.sessionId`, but neither layer can turn it into this
header:
section: Why a plugin is needed at all

text:
dsh-opencode-session-header README · Why a plugin is needed at all：| layer | why it cannot |
| --- | --- |
| provider profile (`settings.yaml`) | `headers:` is a *static* map; one value would collapse every conversation onto one routing bucket and destroy prompt-cache locality |
| DSH's `llm/stream` waterfall | `next()` takes no options, and `GenerateOptions` has no `headers` field |
| pi-ai itself | its session-affinity header is gated behind `compat.sendSessionAffinityHeaders`, which no OpenCode route sets — and DSH classifies that switch as `withhold`, so `settings.yaml` cannot enable it |
section: Why a plugin is needed at all

text:
dsh-opencode-session-header README · Why a plugin is needed at all：So the id is present in the request all the way to the adapter and then dropped.
This plugin re-attaches it at the last point where the request's header map is
still an argument.
section: Why a plugin is needed at all

text:
dsh-opencode-session-header README · Scope: every `opencode-go…` route：The scope is one fixed prefix — not a list, and not a configurable pattern:

```js
export const SCOPED_ROUTE_PREFIX = 'opencode-go';   // matched case-insensitively
export const SCOPED_ROUTE_PATTERN = 'opencode-go*'; // how the status report names it
```

dsh-opencode-session-header README · Scope: every `opencode-go…` route：So the builtin `opencode-go`, this deployment's `opencode-go-custom`, a future
`opencode-go-eu`, and any other route whose key starts with `opencode-go` are
labelled the moment such a route is registered — no configuration and no new
release. Everything else is left byte-for-byte alone, **including other routes
served by the same adapter instance**: `opencode-zen` (a different gateway
contract), `my-opencode-go` (the prefix is anchored at the start), `opencode`,
`deepseek`.

dsh-opencode-session-header README · Scope: every `opencode-go…` route：There is deliberately no `routes:` / `optInRoutes:` / `skipApis:` key: the scope is
a code constant, so a configuration mistake cannot send a gateway-specific header
to a provider that never asked for it. A configuration attempt is rejected with an
error that says exactly where the line falls.

dsh-opencode-session-header README · Scope: every `opencode-go…` route：This is enforced per **model call**, not per adapter: the plugin hooks the pi-ai
adapter, and the decision reads the route key on the model descriptor pi-ai
received. The test suite asserts both directions on the same adapter instance —
an `opencode-go-eu` route labelled, an `opencode-zen` route untouched.

dsh-opencode-session-header README · How it works：```
GenerateOptions.sessionId
  └─ PiAiAdapter#streamWithSnapshot(options, snapshot)   ← the plugin wraps this
       └─ snapshot.models.streamSimple(model, ctx, { …, headers })   ← and this
            └─ pi-ai merges `headers` into the HTTP client's headers last

dsh-opencode-session-header README · How it works：1. `ctx.llm`'s route map is swept for the adapter instances that serve model
   calls. Every pi-ai shaped adapter is wrapped — at its one dispatch choke point
   and on its class, so a later instance is covered too. The scope decides on the
   call, so hooking broadly cannot add the header narrowly.
2. The wrapped call instruments the snapshot's model collection, which is the
   last object holding the request's `headers` map as an argument.
3. That map gets the conversation id, and pi-ai receives a **copy** of the
   options — the adapter's own request object is never mutated.

dsh-opencode-session-header README · How it works：Both hooks are published under `Symbol.for` keys, so the objects stay
indistinguishable from untouched ones to anything that enumerates them, and a
second sweep is a no-op instead of a growing wrapper chain. The class hook is what
covers a new instance after an HMR reload; the registry event
(`llm/adapters-updated`) plus two bounded sweeps cover a route that registers
after this plugin mounts.

dsh-opencode-session-header README · How it works：Nothing is fabricated: a call with no conversation id keeps the deployment's
static headers exactly as they are, unless `sessionlessFallback` lets it borrow
the id of the conversation that initiated it — an auxiliary session-title or
compaction call belongs to a conversation even when it does not say so.

dsh-opencode-session-header README · Value modes：| mode | value | when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `auto` *(default)* | bare UUID, except on `openai-responses` where it is the raw `session-<uuid>` | the Responses implementation already sends `session_id: session-<uuid>` itself, so `auto` makes both headers name the **same** conversation instead of splitting it across two routing buckets |
| `uuid` | bare `05681fd4-…` | the gateway's own documentation; what the patch script sent |
| `id` | raw `session-05681fd4-…` | the gateway accepts this form too |

dsh-opencode-session-header README · Value modes：`auto` matters for this deployment specifically: `opencode-go-custom` is
configured as `api: openai-responses`.

dsh-opencode-session-header README · Install：```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:mathangler/dsh-opencode-session-header
```

That runs pnpm in the profile, appends this package to `dsh.profile.bundles`, and
folds in the row from `cordis.patch.yml` — no manual edit. Then **restart the
whole `dsh` process**, not just the session: the bundle is already loaded in
memory, so the plugin only takes effect on a fresh `dsh` / `dsh web`.

dsh-opencode-session-header README · Install：- Targets DSH `0.2.1-rc.2` (verified) and the `0.1.5` / `0.1.6` line before it. It
  finds the adapter by shape rather than by import, so a bundle that still has
  `PiAiAdapter#streamWithSnapshot` keeps working.
- To update later, remove first — pnpm will not re-resolve a moved `github:`
  HEAD while the spec is unchanged:

```bash
  dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-opencode-session-header
  dsh plugin --profile web add github:mathangler/dsh-opencode-session-header
  ```

dsh-opencode-session-header README · Install：- On restricted networks `github.com` itself may be unreachable while installs
  still work: pnpm fetches the tarball from `codeload.github.com`.
- There is no build step and no lifecycle script, so nothing asks for a build
  approval — the source in `lib/` is what runs.

dsh-opencode-session-header README · What the Plugins page shows (icon, English / Chinese)：DSH renders a plugin's icon, title and description from the package's display
metadata, read by its own `readPluginMeta()`: the artwork from an exported
`./icon`, the text from `locale/<language>.json` resolved per the active locale
(`locale.resolveText()` walks the active language's fallback chain, `zh` → `en`).
This plugin ships all three:

| `locale/en.json` | `OpenCode session header` and its one-sentence English description |

text:
dsh-opencode-session-header README · What the Plugins page shows (icon, English / Chinese)：Both languages carry their own curated title and description, so neither falls
back to the npm `description` (`package.json` keeps that longer text for npm
itself). That symmetry is deliberate: relying on the fallback is what leaves one
language with a hand-written card and the other with a package blurb.

Switching the UI language (**Settings → General → Language**) switches the text
with it; no configuration of this plugin is involved, and no restart is needed.
section: What the Plugins page shows (icon, English / Chinese)

text:
dsh-opencode-session-header README · What the Plugins page shows (icon, English / Chinese)：- **`locale/en.json` is the baseline.** The reader finds the directory by
  resolving `<package>/locale/en.json` and then scans it, so deleting the English
  file silently discards every other dictionary.
- **`exports` and `files[]` decide whether the metadata exists at all.** Both the
  locale resources and `./icon` are resolved through Node's exports map, and only
  `files[]` reaches a published tarball.
- **An icon is SVG, PNG, JPEG or WebP, at most 256 KiB, inside the package.**
  `test/locale.test.mjs` asserts all of this, and asserts DSH's real reader
  returns the `{ en, zh }` map plus this package's icon byte for byte —
  including the case where the English baseline is missing.
section: What the Plugins page shows (icon, English / Chinese)

text:
dsh-opencode-session-header README · Configuration：Nothing is required: every `opencode-go…` route is covered on install.
To change the policy, override the row by id in the profile's own patch layer
(`~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`):

```yaml
- id: opencode-session-header
  config:
    value: uuid              # auto | uuid | id
    sessionlessFallback: false

Unknown keys are an error, not a silent no-op — a typo would otherwise look
exactly like a gateway that still refuses the request.

dsh-opencode-session-header README · Verify it is working：The authoritative check is the status endpoint — one authenticated same-origin
GET (it is fenced by the platform's own trust check; an unauthenticated caller
gets `401` with an empty body):

```
GET /opencode-session-header/status
```

Read `value.hooked`, `value.counters` and `value.diagnostics`:

```jsonc
{
  "scope": ["opencode-go*"],
  "header": "x-opencode-session",
  "hooked": { "adapters": 1, "prototypes": 1, "collections": 1,

dsh-opencode-session-header README · Verify it is working：- `hooked.adapters: 0` or a diagnostic — the registry was not reachable, and the
  header is **not** being added. That is reported loudly at boot, never silently.
- `hooked.routesInScope: []` — no route in this profile begins with the prefix.
- `counters.attached: 0` with `calls: 0` — no model call has happened yet; no
  credential is needed to see the hook, but the counters only move on real
  traffic.
- `preview` evaluates two routes inside the prefix (`opencode-go`,
  `opencode-go-custom`) and two outside it (`opencode-zen`, `deepseek`) against
  every protocol, so it shows both the decision and exactly where the line falls
  — the quickest way to confirm a `value` mode change.

dsh-opencode-session-header README · Verify it is working：The plugin also reports through the host logger (`ctx.logger.info` for a
successful hook, `ctx.logger.error` when the LLM registry cannot be reached).
Note that a real `dsh web` boot does **not** surface `ctx.logger.info` on stdout —
checked on this machine — so use the endpoint rather than the terminal as your
answer.

dsh-opencode-session-header README · Evidence：Four suites, 44 checks, all green against this machine's
`dsh 0.2.1-rc.2` / pi-ai `1.3.0`:

```bash
node test/session-header.test.mjs   # 19
node test/adapter.test.mjs          # 10
node test/host.test.mjs             # 11
node test/locale.test.mjs           #  4

(`node --test test/` works too where the environment allows spawning child
processes; each file also runs directly, in-process.)

dsh-opencode-session-header README · Evidence：| suite | what it proves |
| --- | --- |
| `test/session-header.test.mjs` (19) | the policy: scope, value modes, never fabricate, no mutation of the adapter's object, hook idempotence and exact restore, counters on every branch |
| `test/adapter.test.mjs` (10) | the **real installed** `PiAiAdapter` driven with pi-ai's own `fauxProvider`: the header reaches the exact `SimpleStreamOptions.headers` map that pi-ai's `createClient` merges last, on the direct `stream()` path and on the prepared-call path the agent loop uses — with a control run that proves the environment alone adds nothing, and a five-route run that pins the prefix boundary (`opencode-go-eu` labelled; `opencode-zen`, `my-opencode-go`, `deepseek` untouched) |
| `test/host.test.mjs` (11) | the publication contract, the defensive registry lookup, the plugin wiring (including a composition with no web server), the late-registering registry path, and the endpoint's fence/method/path handling |
| `test/locale.test.mjs` (4) | the display metadata: the dictionaries' shape and language ids, the `exports`/`files[]` entries that make them reachable and shipped, DSH's **real reader** re

dsh-opencode-session-header README · Evidence：Booting a real `dsh web` with this plugin loaded (throwaway `DSH_HOME`, junctions
instead of pnpm) confirmed the part no unit test can: `ctx.llm.adapters` is
reachable in a live process, the hook lands on the live adapter
(`hooked.adapters: 1`, `routesInScope: ["opencode-go", "opencode-go-custom"]`),
the endpoint answers `200` with the profile's cookie and `401` without it, and
`diagnostics` is empty.

dsh-opencode-session-header README · What it deliberately does not do：- It does not patch the install, any bundle on disk, or global `fetch`.
- It does not touch, wrap, or inspect any adapter that is not pi-ai shaped, and it
  never adds a header to a route outside the prefix.
- It cannot label a call that carries no conversation id *and* has no initiating
  agent in scope; such a call is left exactly as the deployment configured it.
section: What it deliberately does not do

text:
dsh-opencode-session-header README · Files：- `lib/session-header.js` — the transport-free core: policy, the per-call
  transform, the hooks, the status report.
- `lib/index.js` — the Cordis host half: registry sweep, logging, the read-only
  status endpoint.
- `locale/en.json`, `locale/zh.json` — the title and description DSH lists for
  this plugin, one file per language.
- `icon.svg` — the glyph DSH lists for this plugin, in the house style.
- `test/` — the four suites above.
- `cordis.patch.yml` — the profile bundle patch (one row).

dsh-opencode-session-header README · Files：Both `lib/` files import only `node:` builtins and each other. That is not a
style choice: a plugin installed with `dsh plugin add file:<dir>` is *linked* into
the profile and resolves modules from its own directory, so a bare
`import '@deepseek-ai/…'` would break at exactly the load it is needed for — and
a test asserts the invariant rather than trusting it.
